premise: Lawndale's defining employer shuts down and the town starts to die; Daria's reflexive mockery curdles into something like grief for a place she spent years pretending not to belong to.

A Lawndale High teacher dies mid-semester and the school stages a grotesque performance of grief (memorial merch, a 'healing assembly'); Daria's refusal to perform mourning reads as heartless until she finds the one honest thing to say.
Daria spends the movie shadowing a working-class classmate whose life leaves no room for irony, slowly exposing her detachment as a luxury she could always afford.

When Quinn's carefully built social identity collapses overnight, Daria finds her sister's shallowness was its own survival strategy and that her sharpest tools are useless for someone else's real pain.
Jake's heart scare drags Daria from family observer to reluctant participant, forcing her to feel something for the anxious, broken man she's only ever found embarrassing.
A decade later a quietly defeated adult Daria takes a teaching job at Lawndale High and realizes she's become the authority figure her teenage self would have eviscerated.
Developers rebrand Lawndale a trendy 'authentic' suburb and Daria is horrified to find her own ironic sensibility has become the marketing language pricing out everyone who made the place real.
An ice storm traps the Morgendorffers for three days with no power and no screens, forcing the family to actually be a family with nothing to hide behind.
Daria's cynical zine gets her hired writing obituaries for the local paper, and writing honestly about strangers' finished lives cracks her certainty that nothing matters.
Jodie's perfectionist machine seizes up and she vanishes; Daria, the only one who saw it coming, must decide whether watching from the sidelines made her a witness or an accomplice.
Broke before college, Daria takes the most degrading seasonal job in Lawndale and finds the mall's dying rituals weirdly moving.
At the ten-year reunion everyone became exactly who Daria predicted, and the smugness of being right curdles into realizing she predicted nothing for herself.
A horror outbreak hits Lawndale and Daria narrates the apocalypse with unbothered contempt.
The special is staged as a full musical of Daria's senior year.
Daria reluctantly goes to prom and learns to let loose.
Daria, Jane, and Tom in a romantic triangle that tears the friendship apart.
Daria joins Mystik Spiral's doomed van tour and watches arrested-development up close.
Helen's firm asks her to do something quietly unethical; Daria watches her workaholic mother's principles get tested and sees where her own moral lines came from.
The whole special is assembled from Lawndale High's own surveillance and AV-club footage.
Ms. Li's surveillance empire faces a scandal and she recruits Daria to help save her job.
Daria is forced to give the graduation speech.
Daria has to babysit a relentlessly sincere kid who sees right through her act.
A classmate's sudden death shatters Lawndale's denial, and Daria's honesty becomes the only thing anyone can stand — then can't.
Daria's estranged, dying grandmother moves in, and the family's least sentimental member becomes her unlikely confidante.
The paper accidentally runs Daria's obituary; watching the town react to her 'death' tells her exactly how invisible she chose to be.
The teachers strike and the school becomes a daycare-shell; Daria's apathy is tested when actual injustice has a side to take.
Daria's sarcastic class-assignment letters to a sister-city pen pal become a real correspondence that exposes how parochial her contempt has been.
Daria takes a summer census job and is forced into every house in Lawndale she's only ever judged from outside.
Daria fakes leaving town to see who notices, and the experiment goes wrong when people grieve.
A record heatwave melts Lawndale's routines and tempers; over one blistering week the veneer comes off everyone and Daria watches.
Daria reluctantly poses for Jane's make-or-break portfolio and confronts being truly seen.
Daria inherits a derelict property in town and has to decide whether to care about something she actually owns.
Assigned to write Lawndale's bicentennial history, Daria uncovers the town's buried, unflattering past and must decide whether honesty is a service or a cruelty.
Awake for the movie's runtime, Daria narrates a single unraveling sleepless night in Lawndale.
A transfer student who is genuinely, disarmingly kind befriends Daria, and kindness turns out to be harder to dismiss than hostility.
Daria gets called for real jury duty the summer before college, and the closed room forces her to convert opinions into consequences.
A charismatic substitute makes nihilism cool and trendy, cheapening Daria's worldview into a fad she has to disown.
A flood destroys the Lane house and Jane moves in with the Morgendorffers, stress-testing the one relationship Daria can't be ironic about.
Lawndale stages a maudlin charity telethon and Daria, conscripted to run it, has to make sincerity work without lying.
Quinn becomes a minor influencer and casts Daria as the 'ugly authentic sister' in her content, monetizing her as a foil in her own family.
A documentary crew films 'typical American teens' at Lawndale and Daria becomes their reluctant star.
Daria's college essay is rejected for being too cynical and she must learn to write what admissions wants.
